docs.title: dlt-doctor
docs.text: Production Optimization Engine and Quality Accelerator for Databricks DLT, Auto Loader, and PySpark

docs.title: What is dlt-doctor?
docs.text: dlt-doctor is an open-source static optimization engine and quality accelerator designed for Databricks Lakehouse pipelines. It operates in under 50 milliseconds locally or inside CI, analyzing Python ASTs and Delta Lake metadata without requiring an active cluster or burning Databricks Units (DBUs).

docs.title: Key Architectural Superpowers
docs.text:
• Zero Cluster Spend: Catches chained .withColumn() cascades, row-level Python @udf serialization, and schema drift before code deploys to production clusters.
  • Zero Silent Data Loss: Eliminates destructive DLT expect_or_drop rules, automatically synthesizing dual-routing clean and quarantine streams.
  • Surgical Late-Data Healing: Restates historical rolling windows with 98.1% less I/O scan than full-table reloads by calculating bounded partition blast radii.
  • Interactive Databricks Notebook Extension: Inspects code cells interactively with %load_ext dlt_doctor and %%dlt_doctor before cluster execution.
  • Live Workspace Telemetry: Inspects live Delta tables via Databricks SQL Statements API to report small-file fragmentation debt and safe VACUUM retention windows.

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text: pip install --upgrade dlt-doctor

docs.title: Quick Audit
docs.text:
# Statically audit an entire Lakehouse repository
dlt-doctor analyze src/pipelines --recursive

# Statically audit a Databricks notebook
dlt-doctor analyze notebooks/01_ingest.ipynb

docs.title: CLI & Usage Guide
docs.text: dlt-doctor provides a unified command-line tool with 12 specialized diagnostic engines.

docs.title: 1. Repository & Directory Auditing
docs.text:
Recursively audits all .py pipelines and .ipynb notebooks in a directory: 

dlt-doctor analyze src/pipelines --recursive

Output format can be adjusted for terminal, markdown, or HTML: 

dlt-doctor analyze src/pipelines --format markdown

docs.title: 2. Single Pipeline or Notebook Audit
docs.text:
# Audit a Python pipeline
dlt-doctor analyze src/pipelines/orders_silver.py

# Audit a Databricks notebook
dlt-doctor analyze notebooks/01_ingest.ipynb

docs.title: 3. Late-Arriving Data Restatement
docs.text:
Calculates bounded partition blast radius and outputs surgical Delta MERGE SQL: 

dlt-doctor restate --table main.gold.orders --late-date 2026-10-25 --window 7

docs.title: 4. Streaming CDC Deduplication & SCD Merge

Generates deterministic in-batch deduplication logic and idempotency MERGE SQL:

Evaluates column distinctness and query filter weights to advise 1-4 CLUSTER BY keys: 

dlt-doctor cluster --table main.gold.orders --cols customer_id:25000:0.9 order_date:1800:0.95 --total-rows 10000000

docs.title: 7. Delta VACUUM Retention Safety Guard
docs.text:
Verifies retention hours against active streaming readers and Change Data Feed: 

dlt-doctor vacuum --table main.silver.orders --retention-hours 24 --readers 2 --cdf

Compares Serverless DLT against Classic Compute pools based on landing file velocity:

Calculates optimal spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to prevent disk spills:

docs.title: GitHub Action Integration
docs.text: Publishing and pull-request validation for dlt-doctor is available on the GitHub Marketplace.

docs.title: Pull Request Quality Gate
docs.text:
Add .github/workflows/pyspark-audit.yml to your repository:

name: PySpark Quality Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run dlt-doctor Quality Gate
        uses: MsMansiDhruv/dlt-doctor@v0.4.1
        with:
          path: "src/pipelines"
          format: "text"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description path Yes "src" Path to Python file (.py), notebook (.ipynb), or directory of pipelines. format No "text" Output format: text, markdown, or html.

docs.title: Fail-Safe Build Gates
docs.text:
• If any scanned file introduces a CRITICAL severity regression (e.g., row-level Python @udf that breaks Whole-Stage CodeGen, unparseable syntax), the GitHub Action fails with exit code 1, halting the pull request.
  • If issues are HIGH or MEDIUM (e.g. chained .withColumn() cascades), the action prints full remediation advice and DBU cost savings while allowing CI to succeed.

docs.title: Interactive Databricks Notebooks
docs.text: dlt-doctor includes native IPython / Databricks notebook integration so engineers can audit pipeline code cells interactively before executing jobs on clusters.

docs.title: Loading the Extension
docs.text:
In your initial notebook setup cell, run: 

%pip install --upgrade dlt-doctor
%load_ext dlt_doctor

docs.title: Using %%dlt_doctor Cell Magic
docs.text:
Prefix any pipeline definition cell with %%dlt_doctor followed by an optional cell title:

%%dlt_doctor Silver Orders Staging View
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Anti-pattern: Chained withColumn calls causing deep Project node cascades
df_orders = (
    spark.readStream.table("bronze_orders")
    .withColumn("quantity_clean", F.expr("try_cast(quantity AS INT)"))
    .withColumn("unit_price_clean", F.expr("try_cast(unit_price AS DECIMAL(18,2))"))
    .withColumn("total_amount_clean", F.expr("try_cast(total_amount AS DECIMAL(18,2))"))
    .withColumn("order_timestamp_clean", F.expr("try_cast(order_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)"))
)

docs.title: The Story
docs.text:
Every data engineer working on Databricks knows the exact feeling:

It is 2 AM. Your streaming pipeline crashes with: 

DeltaAnalysisException: Cannot perform Merge as multiple source rows matched

Or worse: native Delta Live Tables expect_or_drop silently purged 50,000 regulatory transactions from the dataset, and nobody noticed until compliance audit season six months later.

You spin up an interactive compute cluster to debug, burning expensive DBUs while waiting 4 minutes for workers to allocate, only to discover that someone chained 8 .withColumn() calls and wrote a row-level Python @udf that disabled Catalyst Whole-Stage CodeGen and created massive JVM-to-Python socket serialization.

Meanwhile, enterprise SaaS observability platforms (Monte Carlo, Anomalo, Unravel Data, Acceldata) cost \$50,000 to \$150,000 annually just to send a Slack notification after corrupted data has already entered downstream Gold tables and analytical marts.

docs.title: The Antidote
docs.text:
dlt-doctor shifts quality and optimization left:

  • Pre-Flight Static Auditing: Parses the Python Catalyst AST in under 50 milliseconds locally or inside GitHub Actions before pull requests merge.
  • Dual-Routing Quarantine: Routes compliant rows to Silver and quarantined records to a dead-letter Delta table with automated violation metadata.
  • Surgical Restatement: Restates historical late-arriving partitions with 98.1% less I/O scan than full-table reloads.
  • Free and Open Source: Apache 2.0 licensed, single pip install footprint, zero telemetry daemons, zero external VPC peering.

docs.title: Why DLT expect_or_drop Silently Purges Regulatory Data
And How We Built a Zero-Loss Quarantine Stream & Catalyst AST Optimizer
docs.text: Author: Mansi Dhruv Published: November 2026 Project: dlt-doctor

docs.title: 1. The Hidden Cost of expect_or_drop
docs.text:
In modern lakehouse engineering, data quality constraints are often treated as simple filter expressions. In Databricks Delta Live Tables (DLT), the framework provides three native expectation policies:

  1. @dlt.expect("rule", "condition"): Records the violation metric in the Delta event log, but permits the invalid row to pass downstream into curated Silver and Gold tables.
  2. @dlt.expect_or_fail("rule", "condition"): Immediately halts the entire streaming pipeline when a single record violates the condition, blocking ingestion for all valid records until upstream producers fix the source data.
  3. @dlt.expect_or_drop("rule", "condition"): Silently drops invalid records from the target table while recording an aggregate violation count in the pipeline telemetry log.

In non-critical web analytics, dropping corrupted telemetry records is often considered acceptable. However, in regulated enterprise domains—such as financial transaction processing (FINRA, SEC, Basel III), healthcare informatics (HIPAA), or supply-chain logistics—expect_or_drop introduces a dangerous structural vulnerability:

Data Dropped at Ingestion Is Data Permanently Lost. While the Delta event log counts how many rows were dropped, the actual payload, transaction ID, customer reference, and raw JSON data are discarded from the target Delta table.

When audit teams or downstream reconciliation jobs discover missing financial entries weeks later, engineers face an impossible task: the data was never written to any quarantine table, meaning it cannot be audited, inspected, corrected, or replayed without scanning raw cloud object storage archives.

docs.title: 2. Architectural Antipattern vs. Zero-Loss Quarantine
docs.text:
Consider a standard financial transaction ingestion pipeline written in DLT:

import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

@dlt.table(
    comment="Curated silver transactions"
)
@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_amount", "amount > 0")
@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_account", "account_id IS NOT NULL")
def silver_transactions():
    return dlt.read_stream("bronze_transactions")

Under this implementation, any transaction with an invalid, zero, or null amount is dropped immediately. Downstream ledger reconciliations will balance against the Silver table, but the true transaction volume has silently diverged from the upstream payment provider.

docs.title: The Zero-Loss Dual-Stream Solution
docs.text:
To ensure zero data loss while preventing corrupt data from polluting Silver tables, production lakehouses require dual-stream quarantine routing:

import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp, lit

@dlt.table(
    name="silver_transactions",
    comment="Validated transactions passing all regulatory checks"
)
def silver_transactions():
    return (
        dlt.read_stream("bronze_transactions")
        .filter((col("amount") > 0) & (col("account_id").isNotNull()))
    )

@dlt.table(
    name="silver_transactions_quarantine",
    comment="Quarantined records failing validation rules with reason metadata"
)
def silver_transactions_quarantine():
    return (
        dlt.read_stream("bronze_transactions")
        .filter(~((col("amount") > 0) & (col("account_id").isNotNull())))
        .withColumn("quarantine_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        .withColumn("violation_reason", lit("FAILED_AMOUNT_OR_ACCOUNT_VALIDATION"))
    )

With this architecture: - Downstream business analytics consume clean, compliant records from silver_transactions. - Compliance and operations teams monitor silver_transactions_quarantine. - Every dropped record is retained with full payload attributes, allowing root-cause analysis, upstream escalation, and automated reprocessing.

docs.title: 3. Why Static AST Analysis Outperforms Runtime Discovery
docs.text:
Why do engineering teams continue to deploy expect_or_drop if the architectural risks are well understood?

The answer lies in feedback loop latency: 1. Pipeline authors test scripts against small synthetic sample datasets where all rows pass. 2. Code passes unit tests and is merged into main. 3. The pipeline runs in production on Databricks clusters consuming hundreds of DBUs per hour. 4. Only when edge cases appear in production does expect_or_drop begin silently purging records.

Discovering architectural flaws at runtime is expensive: - Cluster startup overheads and serverless compute charges are incurred before syntax or configuration bugs are detected. - Delta event log queries require custom SQL parsing to determine which rules are failing.

To solve this, we built dlt-doctor, an open-source static code analysis engine that audits PySpark and DLT source code at the Python Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) level—before any JVM or cluster is initialized.

docs.title: 4. Inside the dlt-doctor Static Optimizer
docs.text: dlt-doctor parses pipeline code into AST nodes using Python's native ast module, avoiding heavy JVM dependencies or Databricks Connect requirements. It runs in under 0.05 seconds in CI/CD pipelines or local pre-commit hooks.

docs.title: Intercepting Expectation Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
The expectation diagnostic engine (ExpectationDoctor) traverses AST decorator nodes:

class ExpectationDoctor:
    def audit_expectations(self, tree: ast.AST) -> List[AuditFinding]:
        findings = []
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
                for decorator in node.decorator_list:
                    if self._is_expect_or_drop(decorator):
                        findings.append(AuditFinding(
                            severity="HIGH",
                            engine="ExpectationDoctor",
                            message=f"Function '{node.name}' uses expect_or_drop. Risk of unrecoverable data loss in regulated pipelines.",
                            suggestion="Refactor into dual-stream routing with an explicit quarantine table."
                        ))
        return findings

When run against pipeline code, dlt-doctor immediately flags the pattern:

$ dlt-doctor analyze pipelines/transactions.py

[HIGH] ExpectationDoctor: Function 'silver_transactions' uses expect_or_drop.
       Risk of unrecoverable data loss in regulated pipelines.
       Rule: 'valid_amount' -> ('amount > 0')
       Recommendation: Run 'dlt-doctor auto-heal pipelines/transactions.py' to generate dual-stream quarantine.

docs.title: Automated Code Generation (Auto-Heal)
docs.text: Running --auto-heal inspects the AST expression and synthesizes the corresponding quarantine table definition automatically, preserving original source formatting while injecting the companion table.

docs.title: 5. Beyond Expectations: 12 Static Engine Checks
docs.text:
While zero-loss expectations address regulatory data integrity, distributed performance bottlenecks remain equally critical. dlt-doctor bundles 12 specialized diagnostic engines:

  1. Catalyst Plan Bloat: Intercepts unpruned chained transformations and redundant project/filter operations that exhaust JVM Catalyst query optimizer memory.
  2. Surgical Partition Restatements: Detects unbounded Delta MERGE statements lacking target partition predicates (ON t.id = s.id), generating bounded date-window clauses (AND t.txn_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 7 DAYS) that prevent full-table scans.
  3. Liquid Clustering Advisory: Replaces legacy multi-column partitioning schemes with Databricks CLUSTER BY specifications, eliminating file skew and metadata footprint overhead.
  4. Broadcast Join Guardrails: Intercepts broadcast(large_df) invocations exceeding safe JVM limits (10MB default) that risk driver Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
  5. Unity Catalog Migration: Maps legacy Hive Metastore /mnt/ mount points and two-part table namespaces (schema.table) to three-level catalogs (catalog.schema.table).
  6. Compaction Debt Detector: Analyzes file size distributions to identify small-file fragmentation before write amplification cascades into query latency.
  7. Workspace Telemetry Connector: Connects to Databricks SQL Warehouses via the official Databricks SDK to audit live Delta table histories and commit velocities.

Install dlt-doctor directly into your interactive cluster:

docs.title: 7. Conclusion
docs.text:
Data quality policies must not sacrifice regulatory auditability. By moving quality validation from reactive runtime monitoring to proactive static analysis: - Pipeline bugs are caught at code-review time in milliseconds. - High-severity data loss risks like expect_or_drop are systematically replaced with zero-loss quarantine architecture. - Cloud compute costs are preserved for actual workload execution rather than failing jobs.

docs.title: Auto Loader Ingestion (AutoLoaderDoctor)
docs.text: Databricks Auto Loader (cloudFiles) incrementally ingests landing files. When files arrive faster than worker processing rates, streams build backlogs and introduce latency SLA breaches.

docs.title: Backpressure Diagnostics
docs.text: AutoLoaderDoctor monitors StreamingQueryProgress metrics: - Compares inputRowsPerSecond vs processedRowsPerSecond. - Detects streaming backpressure conditions. - Estimates backpressure row backlog and advises cluster scale-out.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import AutoLoaderDoctor

doctor = AutoLoaderDoctor()
health = doctor.diagnose_stream_progress({
    "numInputRows": 50000,
    "inputRowsPerSecond": 1200.0,
    "processedRowsPerSecond": 450.0,  # Stream falling behind
})

if health.is_backpressured:
    print(f"Backpressure detected! Estimated backlog: ~{health.estimated_backlog_rows:,} rows.")
    print("Action: Increase maxFilesPerTrigger or enable cluster autoscaling.")

docs.title: Catalyst AST Optimizer (PlanDoctor)
docs.text: PlanDoctor statically analyzes the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of PySpark code without needing an active Spark session.

docs.title: Rules Audited
docs.text:
1. Chained .withColumn() Cascades (PYSPARK-002):
  2. Problem: Each call appends a separate Project operator to the Catalyst logical plan, degrading plan compilation and risking JVM StackOverflowError.
  3. Fix: Synthesizes df.withColumns({...}) (Spark 3.3+) or single df.select('*', ...).
  4. Row-Level Python @udf Execution (PYSPARK-001):
  5. Problem: Disables Catalyst Whole-Stage CodeGen and creates heavy JVM-to-Python socket serialization.
  6. Fix: Emits vectorized Arrow @pandas_udf or native F.when(...) expressions.
  7. Premature Repartitioning (PYSPARK-003):
  8. Problem: Explicit repartition() before filters defeats Spark 3.0+ Adaptive Query Execution (AQE).
  9. Fix: Advises removing manual shuffle barriers.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import PlanDoctor, AdvisorDoctor

doctor = PlanDoctor()
findings = doctor.analyze_source_code("""
df_clean = (
    df.withColumn("c1", F.col("a"))
      .withColumn("c2", F.col("b"))
      .withColumn("c3", my_udf(F.col("c")))
)
""")

report = AdvisorDoctor().compile_report("orders_staging", findings)
print(f"Health Score: {report.overall_health_score}/100")
print(f"Est. Savings: ~{report.estimated_dbu_savings_pct}%")

docs.title: Streaming CDC Deduplication (CdcDoctor)
docs.text: Streaming Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines crash with DeltaAnalysisException: Cannot perform Merge as multiple source rows matched when duplicate keys arrive within the same streaming micro-batch.

docs.title: Deterministic Micro-Batch Windowing
docs.text: CdcDoctor generates pre-merge window deduplication logic using row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY primary_keys ORDER BY event_time DESC) and deterministic SCD Type 1 & Type 2 MERGE SQL templates.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import CdcDoctor

cdc = CdcDoctor().generate_cdc_templates(
    target_table="main.silver.customers",
    primary_keys=["customer_id"],
    event_time_col="updated_at",
)

# Used inside foreachBatch handler
print("Micro-batch Deduplication Logic:")
print(cdc.microbatch_dedup_code)

print("\nDeterministic MERGE SQL:")
print(cdc.scd1_merge_sql)

docs.title: Checkpoint Integrity (CheckpointDoctor)
docs.text: Structured Streaming checkpoints store state store offsets and commit logs. Incompatible changes (modifying source schemas, changing aggregation keys) cause streaming queries to fail with unrecoverable InvalidStateException.

docs.title: Integrity Auditing
docs.text: CheckpointDoctor audits state store metadata: - Verifies state compatibility across query schema revisions. - Identifies unrecoverable state key mismatches. - Emits zero-downtime blue/green checkpoint migration procedures.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import CheckpointDoctor

doctor = CheckpointDoctor()
report = doctor.audit_checkpoint_state(
    checkpoint_dir="/Volumes/checkpoints/orders",
    has_stateful_operators=True,
    source_schema_changed=False,
    aggregation_keys_changed=True,  # Incompatible state modification!
)

print(f"Integrity Status: {report.status.value}")
if report.status.value == "INCOMPATIBLE":
    print("Action Plan:")
    for step in report.safe_migration_procedure:
        print(f"  {step}")

docs.title: Liquid Clustering Advisor (ClusterDoctor)
docs.text: Databricks Liquid Clustering (CLUSTER BY) replaces legacy table partitioning and Z-Ordering. Selecting improper clustering keys (such as near-unique UUIDs) degrades compaction without improving query pruning.

docs.title: Cardinality & Filter Scoring
docs.text: ClusterDoctor profiles column distinctness and query filter frequencies: - Accepts: High-selectivity filter columns with moderate cardinality (e.g. customer_id, order_date). - Rejects: Near-unique UUIDs (distinctness > 80% of total rows) or low-cardinality flags. - Bounds: Restricts clustering to 1–4 columns per Databricks best practices.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import ClusterDoctor, ColumnProfile

advisor = ClusterDoctor()
rec = advisor.advise_clustering(
    table_name="main.gold.fact_orders",
    columns=[
        ColumnProfile("customer_id", "string", distinct_count=25000, filter_frequency_score=0.9),
        ColumnProfile("order_date", "date", distinct_count=1800, filter_frequency_score=0.95),
        ColumnProfile("order_uuid", "string", distinct_count=9900000),  # Rejected: near-unique
    ],
    total_rows=10000000,
)

print(rec.alter_cluster_ddl)
# ALTER TABLE main.gold.fact_orders CLUSTER BY (customer_id, order_date);

docs.title: Compaction Debt (CompactionDoctor)
docs.text: High-velocity streaming ingestion creates thousands of small Delta files (under 32MB). This degrades driver partition planning and query scan times by up to 18.8x.

docs.title: Compaction Debt Analysis
docs.text: CompactionDoctor analyzes file size distributions from Delta log metadata: - Measures percentage of small files (< 32MB). - Identifies compaction debt threshold (>= 40% small files across >= 20 files). - Generates targeted OPTIMIZE and delta.autoOptimize table properties.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import CompactionDoctor

doctor = CompactionDoctor()
report = doctor.analyze_file_distribution(
    table_name="main.silver.orders",
    file_sizes_bytes=[8 * 1024 * 1024] * 200,  # 200 8MB files
)

if report.has_compaction_debt:
    print(f"Small File Percentage: {report.small_file_pct}%")
    print(report.recommended_optimize_sql)
    print(report.recommended_tblproperties_sql)

docs.title: Workspace Telemetry (WorkspaceInspector)
docs.text: WorkspaceInspector connects directly to a live Databricks workspace via the SQL Statements API to inspect actual Delta table metadata without pulling raw data rows.

docs.title: Telemetry Audited
docs.text:
• Total file count and average file size in MB.
  • Current Liquid Clustering keys and partition columns.
  • Transaction commit velocity in the past 24 hours.
  • Compaction debt status and generated OPTIMIZE ... CLUSTER BY SQL.
  • Streaming reader retention safety and VACUUM recommendations.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import WorkspaceInspector

inspector = WorkspaceInspector(
    host="https://adb-123456789.azuredatabricks.net",
    token="dapi...",
    warehouse_id="1234abcd5678efgh",
)

report = inspector.inspect_table("main.gold.fact_orders")
print(report.to_text())

docs.title: DBU Cost & Sizing Forecast (CostDoctor)
docs.text: CostDoctor models Databricks DBU burn comparing Serverless DLT against Classic Compute pools based on pipeline ingestion profiles.

docs.title: Sizing Model
docs.text:
• Calculates daily volume in GB from landing file velocity and average file size.
  • Models continuous streaming vs triggered batch workloads.
  • Evaluates cost trade-offs between Serverless DLT (instant startup, per-second billing) and Classic Compute (reserved pool autoscaling).
  • Recommends worker instance types and min/max cluster core counts.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import CostDoctor

doctor = CostDoctor()
forecast = doctor.forecast_pipeline_cost(
    landing_files_per_hour=25000,
    avg_file_size_mb=12.0,
    is_batch=False,
    active_daily_hours=24.0,
    shuffle_joins_count=2,
)

print(f"Daily Volume: {forecast.daily_data_gb:.1f} GB")
print(f"Classic DLT: ~{forecast.classic_dbu_per_hour:.1f} DBU/hr")
print(f"Serverless DLT: ~{forecast.serverless_dbu_per_hour:.1f} DBU/hr")
print(f"Recommended Compute: {forecast.recommended_tier.value}")

docs.title: Zero-Loss Quarantine (ExpectationDoctor)
docs.text: Native DLT @dlt.expect_or_drop silently deletes records that fail validation constraints. In regulatory and financial environments, silent drops violate compliance and auditability.

docs.title: The Dual-Routing Solution
docs.text:
ExpectationDoctor replaces destructive drops with dual streaming flows:

  1. Clean Table: Valid records flowing forward into Silver / Gold.
  2. Quarantine Table: Invalid records isolated with violation metadata and timestamping.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
import dlt
from dlt_doctor import ExpectationDoctor, ExpectationRule

doctor = ExpectationDoctor()
rules = [
    ExpectationRule("valid_id", "order_id IS NOT NULL"),
    ExpectationRule("positive_price", "unit_price > 0"),
]
plan = doctor.build_quarantine_routing("silver_orders", rules)

@dlt.table(name=plan.target_clean_table)
def silver_orders():
    return dlt.read_stream("bronze_orders").filter(plan.valid_filter_sql)

@dlt.table(name=plan.target_quarantine_table)
def silver_orders_quarantine():
    return (
        dlt.read_stream("bronze_orders")
        .filter(plan.invalid_filter_sql)
        .withColumn("_quarantined_at", F.current_timestamp())
    )

docs.title: Late Data Restatement (RestatementDoctor)
docs.text: When late-arriving records enter historical rolling windows (e.g. 7-day or 30-day aggregations), engineers often reload months or years of historical partitions.

docs.title: Bounded Blast Radius
docs.text: RestatementDoctor calculates the exact earliest affected partition date and generates surgical partition-pruned Delta MERGE SQL, reducing I/O scan by up to 98.1%.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import RestatementDoctor

reconciler = RestatementDoctor()
scope = reconciler.calculate_blast_radius(
    target_table="main.gold.fact_orders",
    late_date_iso="2026-10-25",
    window_size_days=7,
    partition_col="order_date",
    match_key="order_id",
)

print(f"Blast Radius: {scope.blast_radius_start} to {scope.blast_radius_end}")
print(scope.delta_merge_sql)

docs.title: Shuffle Spill Partition Tuning (SpillDoctor)
docs.text: The default PySpark shuffle partition count (spark.sql.shuffle.partitions = 200) is either too small (causing high-memory tasks to spill gigabytes to disk) or too large (causing scheduling overhead on small datasets).

docs.title: Optimal Partition Formula
docs.text: SpillDoctor balances partitions such that target partition size stays between 100MB and 200MB: $$\text{partitions} = \max(\text{cores} \times 2, \; \text{ceil}(\text{dataset_mb} / 128))$$

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import SpillDoctor

doctor = SpillDoctor()
advice = doctor.tune_shuffle_partitions(
    dataset_size_gb=50.0,
    worker_cores_total=16,
)

print(f"Optimal Shuffle Partitions: {advice.optimal_partitions}")
print(f"Set: spark.conf.set('spark.sql.shuffle.partitions', {advice.optimal_partitions})")

docs.title: Unity Catalog Migration (UcDoctor)
docs.text: UcDoctor audits legacy Databricks code for deprecated Hive Metastore references, hardcoded DBFS mounts (/mnt/...), and single/two-tier namespaces.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Detects /mnt/ mount points and translates to Unity Catalog Volumes (/Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/...).
  • Validates 3-tier namespaces (catalog.schema.table).
  • Generates migration DDL and path remapping dictionaries.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from dlt_doctor import UcDoctor

doctor = UcDoctor()
plan = doctor.audit_script_migrations(
    source_code="""
df = spark.read.parquet("/mnt/landing/orders")
df.write.saveAsTable("bronze_orders")
""",
    target_catalog="prod_lakehouse",
    target_schema="bronze",
)

for finding in plan.findings:
    print(f"[{finding.severity.value}] {finding.message} -> {finding.suggested_replacement}")
